steps.title: Distance isn't the reason
steps.say: Good catch: in northern summer Earth is a bit farther from the Sun. Distance changes only about 3%, so it can't cause the seasons.

ops.text:
Good catch! Distance barely matters:
Earth is only about 3% closer or farther.

steps.title: Tilt points one hemisphere at the Sun
steps.say: Earth's tilted axis makes the northern half lean toward the Sun in northern summer, and the southern half lean away.

steps.title: Steep sunlight means more heat
steps.say: Sunlight hits the north at a steep angle, so the energy is concentrated and the days are long. That is why it is hotter there.

ops.text:
Northern summer: the north is tilted toward the Sun.
Sunlight hits steeply and days are long, so it heats up.
